class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content"><span id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#0A3981;">The Key Mathematical Fact: The Derivative Blows Up at Zero</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 27.77 27)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:44.66em;--ltx-fo-height:11.11em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="156.36" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 153.67)" width="617.97"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:44.66em;">
<span id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">To understand this, let us take a step back and look at the derivative of <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(x)=x\log x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)=x\log x</annotation></semantics></math>. Why this <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)</annotation></semantics></math>? That is how the entropy looks! For <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, we can see that:</span></span>
<span id="S3.EGx9" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<span id="S3.Ex29"><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\frac{d}{dx}(x\log x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">d</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\frac{d}{dx}(x\log x)</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex29.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{d}{dx}x\times\log x+\frac{d}{dx}\log x\times x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">d</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.222em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">d</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.222em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{d}{dx}x\times\log x+\frac{d}{dx}\log x\times x</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
<span id="S3.Ex30"><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=1\times\log x+\frac{1}{x}\times x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.222em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.222em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=1\times\log x+\frac{1}{x}\times x</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
<span id="S3.Ex31"><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=1+\log x." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=1+\log x.</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
</span>
<span id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">We now examine what happens as <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> approaches the mysterious value <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></span>
<span id="S3.Ex32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<span><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex32.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lim_{x\rightarrow 0^{+}}1+\log x\rightarrow-\infty," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo></msup></mrow></munder><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{x\rightarrow 0^{+}}1+\log x\rightarrow-\infty,</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
</span>
<span id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">because as <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\rightarrow 0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\rightarrow 0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log x\rightarrow-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log x\rightarrow-\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, and thus <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1+\log x\rightarrow-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1+\log x\rightarrow-\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. In other words, as our variable approaches <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0^{+}</annotation></semantics></math>, the gradients blowup. Therefore, if we were optimising for <math id="S3.SS2.p2.pic1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, every time we get closer to zero, the gradient politely but firmly tells us to move.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Equipped with this realisation, we return to our case that contains the negative entropy regulariser <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(q)</annotation></semantics></math>, which strongly discourages zero probabilities. Conveniently, the gradients make this preference explicit:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\partial}{\partial q(v)}\Omega(q)=1+\log q(v)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\partial}{\partial q(v)}\Omega(q)=1+\log q(v),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">which blows up as we <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(v)</annotation></semantics></math> approaches zero. Hence, our winner is <img src="" id="S3.SS2.p3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_missing ltx_missing_image" alt="[Uncaptioned image]"> … the <span id="S3.SS2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps" style="font-size:70%;--ltx-fg-color:#0D47A1;">ACTIVE</span> case:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{\scriptsize\color[rgb]{0.0508,0.2773,0.6328}ACTIVE}\quad q_{t}^{\star}(v)&gt;0\ \implies\ s_{t}(v)-\lambda\frac{\partial}{\partial q(v)}\Omega(q_{t}^{\star})(v)=\eta." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#0D47A1;" class="ltx_font_smallcaps" mathcolor="#0D47A1" mathsize="0.700em">ACTIVE</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.778em" rspace="0.778em" stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{\scriptsize\color[rgb]{0.0508,0.2773,0.6328}ACTIVE}\quad q_{t}^{\star}(v)&gt;0\ \implies\ s_{t}(v)-\lambda\frac{\partial}{\partial q(v)}\Omega(q_{t}^{\star})(v)=\eta.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.3" class="ltx_p">Let us do some algebra! Replacing the derivative from Equation <a href="#S3.E6" title="In 3.2 From Negative Entropy to Softmax: A Predictable Ending ‣ 3 LLM Decoding Strategies are Different Regularisers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> in our condition, we get:</p>

<p id="S3.SS2.p3.4" class="ltx_p">with the constant <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=e^{-1}e^{-\frac{\eta}{\lambda}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>η</mi><mi>λ</mi></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=e^{-1}e^{-\frac{\eta}{\lambda}}</annotation></semantics></math>. We know that <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{\star}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}^{\star}(v)</annotation></semantics></math> must be a valid probability distribution, and valid probability distributions insist on summing to one. Let us indulge them:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx11" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex38"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex39"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex39.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\implies C=\frac{1}{\sum_{u\in\mathcal{V}}\exp{\left(\frac{s_{t}(u)}{\lambda}\right)}}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>λ</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\implies C=\frac{1}{\sum_{u\in\mathcal{V}}\exp{\left(\frac{s_{t}(u)}{\lambda}\right)}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.5" class="ltx_p">Therefore, our optimal distribution <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\star}_{t}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\star}_{t}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> if we picked <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(q)</annotation></semantics></math> to be the negative entropy regulariser, ends up being:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex40" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex40.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\text{\scriptsize\color[rgb]{0.5,0,0.125}SoftMax Decoders: }\quad q_{t}^{\star}(v)=\frac{\exp{\left({s_{t}(v)}/{\lambda}\right)}}{\sum_{u\in\mathcal{V}}\exp{\left({s_{t}(u)}/{\lambda}\right)}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#800020;" class="ltx_font_smallcaps" mathcolor="#800020" mathsize="0.700em">SoftMax Decoders: </mtext><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{\scriptsize\color[rgb]{0.5,0,0.125}SoftMax Decoders: }\quad q_{t}^{\star}(v)=\frac{\exp{\left({s_{t}(v)}/{\lambda}\right)}}{\sum_{u\in\mathcal{V}}\exp{\left({s_{t}(u)}/{\lambda}\right)}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.6" class="ltx_p">We thus recover the classical softmax decoder directly from our master optimisation problem. In particular, choosing the (negative) Shannon entropy as the regulariser produces the familiar temperature-controlled distribution, with <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> playing exactly the role of the temperature
<math id="S3.SS2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> in the LLM literature.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This demonstrates that softmax decoding is not an independent heuristic, but the optimiser of our abstract objective under an entropic geometry. In this sense, our framework elevates decoding to a higher-level problem definition: different decoders arise from different regularisers. Decoder design becomes regulariser design.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection" style="font-size:120%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">3.3  Trimming the Vocabulary: Top-K Samplers</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Fortunately, extending the results derived above to Top-K samplers requires only minimal additional work. Until now, we have been pretending that the constraint <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> in Equation <a href="#S2.E1" title="In 2.2 Decoding as Distributional Optimisation ‣ 2 Decoding, Sampling and Optimisation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> does not exist. For Top-K, this pretence is no longer sustainable. First, we define the indices of the <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> highest-scoring tokens. We define the set <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{k}\subset\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>⊂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{k}\subset\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math> such that: <span id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">i)</span> <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{V}_{k}|=k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{V}_{k}|=k</annotation></semantics></math>, and <span id="S3.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ii)</span> <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\forall v\in\mathcal{V}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\forall v\in\mathcal{V}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\forall u\notin\mathcal{V}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>u</mi></mrow><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\forall u\notin\mathcal{V}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}(v)\geq s_{t}(u)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}(v)\geq s_{t}(u)</annotation></semantics></math>. This allows the constraint set <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(k)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math> to be a subset of the simplex <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\mathcal{V})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\mathcal{V})</annotation></semantics></math> where tokens outside the top-<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> are forced to have zero probability:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex41" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex41.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(k)}=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V}):q(v)=0,\forall v\notin\mathcal{V}_{k}\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(k)}=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V}):q(v)=0,\forall v\notin\mathcal{V}_{k}\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To ensure we end up with a Softmax over the Top-K candidates, as before, we use the (negative) Shannon entropy as our regulariser <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(q)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q(v)\log q(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(q)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q(v)\log q(v)</annotation></semantics></math>. With this, the objective becomes:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex42" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex42.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{*}=\arg\max_{q\in\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(k)}}\left[\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q(v)s_{t}(v)-\lambda\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q(v)\log q(v)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}^{*}=\arg\max_{q\in\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(k)}}\left[\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q(v)s_{t}(v)-\lambda\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q(v)\log q(v)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Because <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(v)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(v)=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\notin\mathcal{V}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\notin\mathcal{V}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> per our constraint, the summation effectively collapses to the indices in <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex43" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex43.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{*}=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V}_{k})}\left[\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{k}}q(v)s_{t}(v)-\lambda\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}_{k}}q(v)\log q(v)\right]." display="block" q(v)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S3.SS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">Following a similar derivation to that in Section <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 From Negative Entropy to Softmax: A Predictable Ending ‣ 3 LLM Decoding Strategies are Different Regularisers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>, we arrive at Top-K samplers giving us:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex44" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection" style="font-size:120%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">3.4  Mind the Mass: Top-P Sampling</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Top-P (nucleus) sampling adapts the size of the active support set based on the model’s
confidence in the current context. When the model’s distribution is <em id="S3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">flat</em> (high uncertainty),
the nucleus expands to preserve diversity; when it is <em id="S3.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">peaky</em> (high confidence), the nucleus
contracts, filtering out low-probability noise in the long tail.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In our optimisation view, Top-P is obtained by replacing the fixed-cardinality support constraint
of Top-K with a <em id="S3.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">cumulative-mass support constraint</em>. Rather than restricting the decoder to
exactly K tokens irrespective of confidence, Top-P restricts the decoder to the smallest set of
tokens whose <em id="S3.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">model-assigned probability mass</em> exceeds a threshold <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in(0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Defining the nucleus.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the model distribution over next tokens induced by the scores <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. Sort tokens in descending order of <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{t}(v^{(1)})\geq p_{t}(v^{(2)})\geq\cdots." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">≥</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{t}(v^{(1)})\geq p_{t}(v^{(2)})\geq\cdots.</annotation></semantics></math> Define <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> to be the smallest index such that the cumulative mass reaches <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_{t}\!\left(v^{(i)}\right)\geq p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_{t}\!\left(v^{(i)}\right)\geq p</annotation></semantics></math>, and set the nucleus to be<span id="footnote3" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">3</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">3</span>
                
                
                
              If ties occur at the cutoff, we may break them arbitrarily.</span></span></span>:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex45" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex45.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{p}:=\{v^{(1)},\dots,v^{(m)}\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>v</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{p}:=\{v^{(1)},\dots,v^{(m)}\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This induces the context-dependent constraint set <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(p)}:=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V}):q(v)=0,\ \forall v\notin\mathcal{V}_{p}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.667em">,</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(p)}:=\{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V}):q(v)=0,\ \forall v\notin\mathcal{V}_{p}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is a sub-simplex of <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\mathcal{V})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\mathcal{V})</annotation></semantics></math> supported on <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>. To recover the standard Top-P sampler, we again use the (negative) Shannon entropy regulariser, and solve the master objective restricted to <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(p)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(p)}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex46" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex46.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{\star}=\arg\max_{q\in\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(p)}}\Big[\langle q,s_{t}\rangle-\lambda\Omega(q)\Big]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></munder><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}^{\star}=\arg\max_{q\in\mathcal{C}_{t}^{(p)}}\Big[\langle q,s_{t}\rangle-\lambda\Omega(q)\Big].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Because <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(v)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(v)=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\notin\mathcal{V}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\notin\mathcal{V}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, this optimisation is equivalent to optimising over
the simplex <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\mathcal{V}_{p})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\mathcal{V}_{p})</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex47" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex47.m1" class="ltx_Math" q(v)\Big].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">The derivation in Section <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 From Negative Entropy to Softmax: A Predictable Ending ‣ 3 LLM Decoding Strategies are Different Regularisers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> therefore applies verbatim, yielding a softmax distribution renormalised over the nucleus:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex48" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" encoding="application/x-tex">\text{\scriptsize\color[rgb]{0.5,0,0.125}Top-P Decoders: }\quad q_{t}^{\star}(v)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{\exp\!\left(s_{t}(v)/\lambda\right)}{\sum\limits_{u\in\mathcal{V}_{p}}\exp\!\left(s_{t}(u)/\lambda\right)}&amp;\text{if }v\in\mathcal{V}_{p},\\[10.0pt]
0&amp;\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">In words, Top-P sampling first selects a context-dependent nucleus <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> based on
cumulative model probability mass, and then samples from a temperature-controlled softmax
restricted to that nucleus.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection" style="font-size:120%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">3.5  Letting Probabilities Go to Zero: Sparsemax Decoding</h3>

<div id="S3.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While standard Softmax sampling is the standard choice for text generation, it suffers from the “heavy tail” problem: because the derivative of Shannon entropy approaches <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\infty</annotation></semantics></math> as any probability <math id="S3.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(v)</annotation></semantics></math> approaches zero, the optimiser is strictly forbidden from reaching the boundary of the simplex. This forces the model to assign a non-zero, albeit small, probability to every single token in the vocabulary, which can lead to the “tail risk” of sampling nonsensical or hallucinatory tokens.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To solve this without the ad-hoc truncation rules of Top-K or Top-P, we look toward Sparsemax <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>]</cite>. By replacing the logarithmic penalty of entropy with a quadratic penalty, we allow the optimisation to reach the simplex boundary, effectively performing an automated, adaptive truncation that assigns exactly zero probability to low-scoring candidates. We again consider a single decoding step with an empty <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and solve the “Master problem” again. In this special case, we choose the quadratic regulariser:</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(q)=\frac{1}{2}\lVert q\rVert_{2}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in V}q(v)^{2},\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad q_{t}^{\star}=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\langle q,s_{t}\rangle-\frac{\lambda}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo fence="true" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mi>q</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0.1389em">∥</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo lspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>V</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.889em">,</mo><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(q)=\frac{1}{2}\lVert q\rVert_{2}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in V}q(v)^{2},\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad q_{t}^{\star}=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\langle q,s_{t}\rangle-\frac{\lambda}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Please note that in our problem, both conditions in Equation (<a href="#S2.E5" title="In Getting the Inequality Back. ‣ 2.2 Decoding as Distributional Optimisation ‣ 2 Decoding, Sampling and Optimisation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) need to be considered. This is the case since <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega(q)=\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega(q)=\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> allows solutions that are positive but can also equate to zero. Of course, the latter condition is what enables sparsity. Let us first consider the active tokens case, i.e., when <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\star}_{t}(v)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\star}_{t}(v)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. For a token <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\in\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\in\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math>, the active condition can be written as:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx12" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex49"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex49.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\text{\scriptsize\color[rgb]{0.0508,0.2773,0.6328}ACTIVE}\quad s_{t}(v)-\lambda\frac{\partial}{\partial q(v)}\Omega(q^{\star}_{t})(v)=\eta\quad" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#0D47A1;" class="ltx_font_smallcaps" mathcolor="#0D47A1" mathsize="0.700em">ACTIVE</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\text{\scriptsize\color[rgb]{0.0508,0.2773,0.6328}ACTIVE}\quad s_{t}(v)-\lambda\frac{\partial}{\partial q(v)}\Omega(q^{\star}_{t})(v)=\eta\quad</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex49.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\implies\quad s_{t}(v)-\lambda\frac{\partial}{\partial q(v)}\left[\frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q_{t}^{\star}(v)^{2}\right]=\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\implies\quad s_{t}(v)-\lambda\frac{\partial}{\partial q(v)}\left[\frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q_{t}^{\star}(v)^{2}\right]=\eta</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex50"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex50.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\implies s_{t}(v)-\lambda q_{t}^{\star}(v)=\eta." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\implies s_{t}(v)-\lambda q_{t}^{\star}(v)=\eta.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p2.3" class="ltx_p">Solving for <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\star}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\star}(v)</annotation></semantics></math>, we get: <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\star}_{t}(v)=\frac{1}{\lambda}(s_{t}(v)-\eta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>λ</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\star}_{t}(v)=\frac{1}{\lambda}(s_{t}(v)-\eta)</annotation></semantics></math>. Also notice that since we are in the <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{\star}(v)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}^{\star}(v)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, we can, thus, clearly see that <math id="S3.SS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}(v)&gt;\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}(v)&gt;\eta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">

<p id="S3.SS5.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Since this condition holds for a token in which <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\star}_{t}(v)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\star}_{t}(v)=0</annotation></semantics></math>, then we can conclude that: <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}(v)\leq\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}(v)\leq\eta</annotation></semantics></math>. So, essentially, from those two conditions we learned that:</p>
