<p id="S3.SS5.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS5.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">with</span><math id="S3.SS5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\quad[x]_{+}=\max(0,x)=\text{ReLU}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>ReLU</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\quad[x]_{+}=\max(0,x)=\text{ReLU}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. The last remaining ingredient needed to finalise our derivation is determining <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>. To do so, we make use of the constraint that <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q_{t}^{\star}(v)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q_{t}^{\star}(v)=1</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S3.EGx13" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S3.Ex53"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex53.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q^{\star}_{t}(v)=1\quad\implies\quad\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}\frac{1}{\lambda}[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}=1\quad" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>λ</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}q^{\star}_{t}(v)=1\quad\implies\quad\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}\frac{1}{\lambda}[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}=1\quad</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex53.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\implies\quad\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}=\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\implies\quad\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}=\lambda</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S3.Ex54"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.Ex54.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\implies\quad\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}\max(0,s_{t}-\eta)=\lambda." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\implies\quad\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}\max(0,s_{t}-\eta)=\lambda.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p3.4" class="ltx_p">In other words, we need <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> such that the sum of the positive parts equals <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>. As we see, it is challenging to acquire a closed-form solution for <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore, we develop an algorithmic solution. The key idea is that we will assume we know which tokens are active by defining an active set <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(\eta)=\{v\in\mathcal{V}:s_{t}(v)&gt;\eta\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(\eta)=\{v\in\mathcal{V}:s_{t}(v)&gt;\eta\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then, we have: <span id="S3.SS5.p3.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">i)</span> If <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\in\mathcal{S}(\eta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\in\mathcal{S}(\eta)</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}=s_{t}(v)-\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}=s_{t}(v)-\eta</annotation></semantics></math>; and <span id="S3.SS5.p3.4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">ii)</span> If <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v\notin\mathcal{S}(\eta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∉</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v\notin\mathcal{S}(\eta)</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore, those conditions over <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> simplify to a sum over the active set <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(\eta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(\eta)</annotation></semantics></math>, giving us: <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}(s_{t}(v)-\eta)=\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}(s_{t}(v)-\eta)=\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>. Unfortunately, this result is still “implicit” because <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(\eta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(\eta)</annotation></semantics></math> depends on <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math> itself. So, we apply the standard trick of guessing the active set size <math id="S3.SS5.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The key observation is that the
<em id="S3.SS5.p4.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">active</em> tokens are exactly those satisfying <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}(v)&gt;\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}(v)&gt;\eta</annotation></semantics></math>. Consequently, if a token with some score <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}(v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}(v)</annotation></semantics></math> is active, then every token with a larger score must also be active. Therefore, the support of <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{\star}_{t}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{\star}_{t}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> must be a <em id="S3.SS5.p4.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Top-K</em> set for some <math id="S3.SS5.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS5.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{t}^{(1)}\geq s^{(2)}_{t}\geq\cdots\geq s^{(n)}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>≥</mo><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo rspace="0.1389em">≥</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.1389em">⋯</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em">≥</mo><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{t}^{(1)}\geq s^{(2)}_{t}\geq\cdots\geq s^{(n)}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the scores sorted in descending order, where <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n:=|\mathcal{V}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n:=|\mathcal{V}|</annotation></semantics></math>.
Assume that the active set has size <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> and is given by the top-<math id="S3.SS5.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> indices:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex55" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex55.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{k}(\eta)=\{(1),(2),\ldots,(k)\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{k}(\eta)=\{(1),(2),\ldots,(k)\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p5.2" class="ltx_p">Under this hypothesis, the normalisation condition becomes:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex56" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex56.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{v\in\mathcal{S}(\eta)}q_{t}^{\star}(v)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\big(s^{(i)}_{t}-\eta\big)=1," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>λ</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></munderover><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{v\in\mathcal{S}(\eta)}q_{t}^{\star}(v)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\sum_{i=1}^{k}\big(s^{(i)}_{t}-\eta\big)=1,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p5.3" class="ltx_p">since tokens outside <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}_{k}(\eta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}_{k}(\eta)</annotation></semantics></math> contribute zero after the <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\cdot]_{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\cdot]_{+}</annotation></semantics></math> clipping. Defining the prefix sum: <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{k}:=\sum_{i=1}^{k}s^{(i)}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">:=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{k}:=\sum_{i=1}^{k}s^{(i)}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex57" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex57.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1=\frac{1}{\lambda}\big(A_{k}-k\eta\big)\qquad\implies\qquad A_{k}-k\eta=\lambda\qquad\implies\qquad\eta_{k}:=\frac{A_{k}-\lambda}{k}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>λ</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mspace style="width:2em;" width="2em"></mspace><mrow><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1=\frac{1}{\lambda}\big(A_{k}-k\eta\big)\qquad\implies\qquad A_{k}-k\eta=\lambda\qquad\implies\qquad\eta_{k}:=\frac{A_{k}-\lambda}{k}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS5.p5.4" class="ltx_p">Importantly, <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is not an arbitrary choice: it is the <em id="S3.SS5.p5.4.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">unique</em> threshold value that would make
<math id="S3.SS5.p5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{v}q^{\star}_{t}(v)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>v</mi></msub><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{v}q^{\star}_{t}(v)=1</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="S3.SS5.p5.4.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">if</em> the active set were exactly the top <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> tokens. The remaining question is which <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> is self-consistent. The Top-K hypothesis holds precisely when the computed threshold
<math id="S3.SS5.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> separates the top <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> scores from the rest, i.e., <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{(k)}_{t}&gt;\eta_{k}\quad\text{and}\quad s^{(k+1)}_{t}\leq\eta_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>and</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{(k)}_{t}&gt;\eta_{k}\quad\text{and}\quad s^{(k+1)}_{t}\leq\eta_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, with the convention <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{(n+1)}_{t}=-\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{(n+1)}_{t}=-\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. We select any <math id="S3.SS5.p5.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>k</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying the above inequalities, set
<math id="S3.SS5.p5.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=\eta_{k^{\star}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>η</mi><msup><mi>k</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=\eta_{k^{\star}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then recover the optimal distribution via:</p>
<table id="S3.Ex58" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex58.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\text{\scriptsize\color[rgb]{0.5,0,0.125}SparseMax-Style Decoders: }\quad q_{t}^{\star}(v)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\,[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#800020;" class="ltx_font_smallcaps" mathcolor="#800020" mathsize="0.700em">SparseMax-Style Decoders: </mtext><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>λ</mi></mfrac><msub><mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{\scriptsize\color[rgb]{0.5,0,0.125}SparseMax-Style Decoders: }\quad q_{t}^{\star}(v)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\,[s_{t}(v)-\eta]_{+}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_section" style="font-size:144%;">4  Going Beyond Current Decoders</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">So far, our story has been pleasantly “closed-form”. Once we write decoding as a regularised optimisation problem on the simplex, the KKT conditions act like a master key, and classical decoders fall out as special cases. In a complementary direction, prior work has shown that search-based decoding methods (e.g., beam search) can also be reinterpreted as optimising an explicit regularised objective <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>. But this view raises an immediate practical question: what do we do when the optimiser is no longer solvable in one line? The moment we introduce richer regularisers, coupling terms, coverage objectives, or more structured constraints, the distribution <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}^{\star}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}^{\star}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> is still well-defined—but we cannot always write it down analytically. This section switches from deriving decoders to <em id="S4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">computing them</em>. We introduce mirror descent (and mirror ascent) as a principled method tailored to simplex geometry. It preserves non-negativity and normalisation by construction and provides an algorithmic template that solves our master problem even when closed-form solutions are unavailable.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection" style="font-size:120%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">4.1  Why not just run Vanilla (projected) Gradient Ascent on <math id="S4.SS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;" mathcolor="#808080">q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;" mathcolor="#808080" stretchy="false">(</mo><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#808080" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#808080;" mathcolor="#808080" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math>?</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If we look back at our master problem, it is natural to try solving it with a standard tool from constrained optimisation: projected gradient ascent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>. After all, we are maximising a differentiable objective over a convex set (the simplex, possibly intersected with additional constraints). One could take a gradient step
and then project back onto <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\mathcal{V})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\mathcal{V})</annotation></semantics></math>, repeating until convergence. In practice, this approach is indeed feasible, and it is often the first method people reach for. To make this explicit, we write the following optimisation problem and update rule<span id="footnote4" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">4</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">4</span>
              
              
              
            Please notice that we have ignored <math id="footnote4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> for now. We can easily incorporate it again by defining a sub-simplex depending on the <math id="footnote4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\mathcal{V})\subseteq\mathcal{V}\cap\mathcal{C}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo>∩</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\mathcal{V})\subseteq\mathcal{V}\cap\mathcal{C}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></span></span>:</p>
<table id="S4.EGx14" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.Ex59"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><span id="S4.Ex59.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_smallcaps" style="font-size:70%;--ltx-fg-color:#0D47A1;">“Master Problem”</span></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex59.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}f(q),\quad\text{with}\quad f(q)=\langle q,s_{t}\rangle\;-\;\lambda\,\Omega(q)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mtext>with</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.502em">−</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}f(q),\quad\text{with}\quad f(q)=\langle q,s_{t}\rangle\;-\;\lambda\,\Omega(q),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S4.Ex60"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><span id="S4.Ex60.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_smallcaps" style="font-size:70%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">“Projected Gradients”</span></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex60.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\boxed{q_{j+1}=\prod_{\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left(q_{j}+\eta\nabla f(q_{j})\right),}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><menclose notation="box"><mrow><mi>q</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mo movablelimits="false">∏</mo></mstyle><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>(</mo><mi>q</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow></menclose><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\quad\quad\quad\boxed{q_{j+1}=\prod_{\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left(q_{j}+\eta\nabla f(q_{j})\right),}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\prod_{\Delta(\mathcal{V})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\prod_{\Delta(\mathcal{V})}</annotation></semantics></math> denoting the projection onto the simplex.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">What do projected gradients solve?</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We note that the projected ascent step above is also somewhat misguided as it implicitly equips the simplex with an <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> geometry that does not match the way probability distributions behave, especially near the boundary where many tokens should receive exactly zero (or near-zero) mass. This mismatch can lead to unstable updates, overly aggressive redistribution of mass, and “fighting the constraints” at every iteration. This is not a philosophy! We can explicitly characterise this property by understanding that projected gradients are the solution to the following optimisation problem:</p>
<table id="S4.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{j+1}=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\langle\nabla f(q_{j}),q-q_{j}\rangle-\frac{1}{2\eta}\left|\left|q-q_{j}\right|\right|_{2}^{2}\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{j+1}=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\langle\nabla f(q_{j}),q-q_{j}\rangle-\frac{1}{2\eta}\left|\left|q-q_{j}\right|\right|_{2}^{2}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Let us see why! We begin by expanding the terms in Equation (<a href="#S4.E8" title="In What do projected gradients solve? ‣ 4.1 Why not just run Vanilla (projected) Gradient Ascent on 𝑞(⋅)? ‣ 4 Going Beyond Current Decoders" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>):</p>
<table id="S4.EGx15" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\nabla f(q_{j})^{\mathsf{T}}q-\nabla f(q_{j})^{\mathsf{T}}q_{j}-\frac{1}{2\eta}\left(||q||_{2}^{2}-2\langle q,q_{j}\rangle\right)+\frac{1}{2\eta}||q_{j}||_{2}^{2}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Notice from the above that <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\nabla f(q_{j})^{\mathsf{T}}q_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝖳</mi></msup><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla f(q_{j})^{\mathsf{T}}q_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="||q_{j}||_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">||q_{j}||_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> are independent from the optimisation variable <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>. Removing those and multiplying by <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>, we get:</p>
<table id="S4.EGx16" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.Ex64"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex64.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle q_{j+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle q_{j+1}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex64.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\eta\nabla f(q_{j})^{\mathsf{T}}q-\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}+\langle q,q_{j}\rangle\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>arg</mi><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>𝖳</mi></msup><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>q</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em">+</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\eta\nabla f(q_{j})^{\mathsf{T}}q-\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}+\langle q,q_{j}\rangle\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S4.Ex65"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex65.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\langle q,q_{j}+\eta\nabla f(q_{j})\rangle-\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}\right]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>arg</mi><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>q</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\langle q,q_{j}+\eta\nabla f(q_{j})\rangle-\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">If we call <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="y=q_{j}+\eta\nabla f(q_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=q_{j}+\eta\nabla f(q_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>, we get the following optimisation problem:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex66" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex66.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{j+1}=\arg\min_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}-\langle q,y\rangle\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{j+1}=\arg\min_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}-\langle q,y\rangle\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.5" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> is independent of <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>, we can add <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{2}||y||_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}||y||_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> to our minimisation problem to complete the squares, giving us:</p>
<table id="S4.EGx17" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.Ex67"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex67.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle q_{j+1}=\arg\min_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}-\langle q,y\rangle+\frac{1}{2}||y||_{2}^{2}\right]=\arg\min_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\frac{1}{2}\left[||q-y||_{2}^{2}\right]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mstyle stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle q_{j+1}=\arg\min_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}-\langle q,y\rangle+\frac{1}{2}||y||_{2}^{2}\right]=\arg\min_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\frac{1}{2}\left[||q-y||_{2}^{2}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.6" class="ltx_p">From the last line, we see that the projected-gradient update is exactly a Euclidean projection:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex68" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex68.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{j+1}=\prod_{\Delta(\mathcal{V})}(y),\quad\text{where}\quad\prod_{\Delta(\mathcal{V})}(y)=\arg\min_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\frac{1}{2}||q-y||_{2}^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∏</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mtext>where</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∏</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{j+1}=\prod_{\Delta(\mathcal{V})}(y),\quad\text{where}\quad\prod_{\Delta(\mathcal{V})}(y)=\arg\min_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\frac{1}{2}||q-y||_{2}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.7" class="ltx_p">In other words, projected gradient ascent produces the next iterate by choosing the distribution <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> on the simplex that is closest to the unconstrained step <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math> in squared <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> distance. This reveals an important (and often overlooked) fact: projected gradient ascent is not “geometry neutral”: it is the solution to a proximal subproblem with an <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> regulariser, i.e., it implicitly assumes Euclidean geometry. While this is a reasonable choice in <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, it is a poor match for probability distributions on the simplex, which form a constrained manifold whose natural notion of distance is typically divergence-like (e.g., KL) rather than Euclidean. This mismatch is precisely what mirror descent corrects by replacing the squared <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>
proximity term with a Bregman divergence that respects the simplex geometry.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_font_bold ltx_title_subsection" style="font-size:120%;--ltx-fg-color:#808080;">4.2  Bregman Divergences &amp; Mirror Ascent</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If decoding lives on the simplex, then using <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{L}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{L}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> geometry is like doing navigation on the Earth with a flat map: it works locally, but it distorts what “small” moves mean. Mirror ascent <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> replaces this distortion with the right geometry. Instead of measuring steps by squared distance, it measures them by a Bregman divergence <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>ψ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>, induced by a convex potential <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ψ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>. The Bregman divergence is defined as:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex69" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex69.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})=\psi(q)-\psi(q_{j})-\langle\nabla\psi(q_{j}),q-q_{j},\rangle" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>ψ</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})=\psi(q)-\psi(q_{j})-\langle\nabla\psi(q_{j}),q-q_{j},\rangle</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">for a strictly convex and differentiable function <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi:\Delta(\mathcal{V})\rightarrow\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi:\Delta(\mathcal{V})\rightarrow\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is called the distance-
generating (or potential) function. Given <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>ψ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>, we rewrite the problem in (<a href="#S4.E8" title="In What do projected gradients solve? ‣ 4.1 Why not just run Vanilla (projected) Gradient Ascent on 𝑞(⋅)? ‣ 4 Going Beyond Current Decoders" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>) as a Bregman regularised one:</p>
<table id="S4.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{j+1}=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\langle\nabla f(q_{j}),q-q_{j}\rangle-\frac{1}{\eta}\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>η</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>ψ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{j+1}=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\langle\nabla f(q_{j}),q-q_{j}\rangle-\frac{1}{\eta}\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<span id="S4.SS2.p2.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:44.66em;">
<span id="S4.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">It is interesting to see that if we choose <math id="S4.SS2.p2.pic1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi(q)</annotation></semantics></math> to be the Euclidean norm, i.e., <math id="S4.SS2.p2.pic1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi(q)=\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi(q)=\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, we would recover Equation (<a href="#S4.E8" title="In What do projected gradients solve? ‣ 4.1 Why not just run Vanilla (projected) Gradient Ascent on 𝑞(⋅)? ‣ 4 Going Beyond Current Decoders" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>) as a special case of the generalised problem in Equation (<a href="#S4.E9" title="In 4.2 Bregman Divergences &amp; Mirror Ascent ‣ 4 Going Beyond Current Decoders" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>). To show that, we begin by understanding the Bregman divergence:</span></span>
<span id="S4.Ex70" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<span><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex70.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})=\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}||q_{j}||_{2}^{2}-\langle q_{j},q-q_{j}\rangle=\frac{1}{2}||q-q_{j}||_{2}^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo mathcolor="#000000">2</mn><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mrow><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mi mathcolor="#000000">2</mn><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mrow><mo mathcolor="#000000">j</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="false" mathcolor="#000000">|</mo><msubsup><mrow><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi></msub></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{\psi}(q,q_{j})=\frac{1}{2}||q||_{2}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}||q_{j}||_{2}^{2}-\langle q_{j},q-q_{j}\rangle=\frac{1}{2}||q-q_{j}||_{2}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
</span>
<span id="S4.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If we replace this last result into Equation (<a href="#S4.E9" title="In 4.2 Bregman Divergences &amp; Mirror Ascent ‣ 4 Going Beyond Current Decoders" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>), we exactly obtain Equation (<a href="#S4.E8" title="In What do projected gradients solve? ‣ 4.1 Why not just run Vanilla (projected) Gradient Ascent on 𝑞(⋅)? ‣ 4 Going Beyond Current Decoders" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>), which we have shown corresponds to the optimisation problem solved with projected gradient ascent. This goes to say that the problem in Equation (<a href="#S4.E8" title="In What do projected gradients solve? ‣ 4.1 Why not just run Vanilla (projected) Gradient Ascent on 𝑞(⋅)? ‣ 4 Going Beyond Current Decoders" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>) allows us to use a more general notion of divergences
defined through <math id="S4.SS2.p2.pic1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ψ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi</annotation></semantics></math>, giving us the ability to consider manifolds (e.g., simplexes) that go beyond
Euclidean spaces.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Entropic Distance-Generating Functions over the Simplex.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When optimising over a <em id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">simplex</em> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>, the standard choice for the distance-generating function is the entropic potential: <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi(q)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}q^{(i)}\log q^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi(q)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}q^{(i)}\log q^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math>. In here, the resulting Bregman divergence becomes the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence. Therefore, the problem in Equation (<a href="#S4.E9" title="In 4.2 Bregman Divergences &amp; Mirror Ascent ‣ 4 Going Beyond Current Decoders" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>) becomes:</p>
<table id="S4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E10.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="q_{j+1}=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\eta\langle\nabla f(q_{j}),q\rangle-\text{KL}(q||q_{j})\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>arg</mi><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>η</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mtext>KL</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{j+1}=\arg\max_{q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V})}\left[\eta\langle\nabla f(q_{j}),q\rangle-\text{KL}(q||q_{j})\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Now, let us solve the problem in Equation (<a href="#S4.E10" title="In Entropic Distance-Generating Functions over the Simplex. ‣ 4.2 Bregman Divergences &amp; Mirror Ascent ‣ 4 Going Beyond Current Decoders" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>) to get the final form of our update. Noticing that we have a constraint <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i=1}^{n}q^{(i)}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{i=1}^{n}q^{(i)}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and ignoring the positivity constraint <span id="footnote5" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">5</sup>
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">5</span>
                
                
                
              The constraint has been ignored since the log function naturally enforces positivity.</span></span></span> on <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math>, the Lagrangian is defined as:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex71" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

Consider the partial derivative of <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(q,\nu)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(q,\nu)</annotation></semantics></math> for a single component <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math> and set it to zero:</p>
